ranking.note: Raised to P1: the only PR fixing a concrete reported data race (#36515) in the interface external miners already use; leaving it at P2 with the feature PRs would flatten a correctness bug into the same level as enhancements.
Root of the BlockTemplateManager chain (#33922, #36356, #36357 build on it) as well as a measurable CPU/lock-contention win for template polling.
Moved up: it is the only fix for a user-reported failure (#34262) miners hit in normal operation, so it leads the P3 block ahead of tooling and refactors.
Moved up: signed-overflow UB that silently drops prioritised transactions from templates is a template-correctness issue, ranking above cleanups and tests despite the unrealistic trigger.
Moved up: it is the declared base of #36357, so reviewing it first is what makes the user-visible getmininginfo fix mergeable.
Moved down: developer-facing tooling ranks last in this category's ordering, below the behavioural fixes it now sits behind.
Lowered to P4: reviewers confirm the no-mempool lookup path is unreachable in production, making it a contract-consistency tidy-up on par with #36451 rather than a real bug fix.

inconsistencies: Chain: #35581 introduces BlockTemplateManager; #33922 (getMemoryLoad), #36356 (gbt cache) and #36357 (BlockAssembler statics) all depend on that structure. Review #35581 first or the later three will need rebasing.
Chain: #36357 is explicitly based on #36356; #36356 must be reviewed/merged first even though #36357 carries the user-visible getmininginfo fix.
#35598 was extracted from #33922 and only tests behaviour that PR's work exercises; review it alongside or after #33922 rather than standalone.

#35300 (deprecating capnp ordinals on submitBlock/submitSolution) and #36097 (replacing interrupt methods with cancellation arguments) both reshape the Mining capnp interface; their ordinal/signature changes will collide and should be sequenced deliberately. #35300 also overlaps #36525, which touches submitSolution's template locking.
#36132 and #36156 are both small BlockAssembler/lookup edge-case adjustments with near-zero production effect; they can be reviewed together and should not displace the correctness fixes above them.
result.notes: No PR here threatens template validity or fund safety, so the band distribution is deliberately top-light: one P1 (a concrete data race in the live IPC mining interface), four P2 interface/performance projects driven by Stratum v2 needs, and a long P3 tail of genuine but deferrable fixes, tooling and tests. Two items whose benefit is explicitly acknowledged as theoretical or worth a negligible fraction of a block's fees sit at P4.
